To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hK6, a recently discovered kallikrein, and hK10, a previously known kallikreinin, are expressed in pancreatic islets and in pancreatic ducts and may be involved in the processing of pancreatic hormones.
the human kallikrins 6 and hK6 are expressed in the pancreatic islet cells of both the normal and diseased pancreas and that they are co-localized with the pancreatic hormones.
the kallikrein 6 and 9 (hK6, hKK9) genes are located in a cluster on chromosome 19q13.4 and that hK6 expression is up-regulated in prostate cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the localization of the human tissue kallikrein genes hK6 and/or hK10 in the endocrine and exocrine pancreas.
the immunohistochemical localization and the co-expression of the newly identified kallikrein genes hK6 and 10, in the endocrine pancrea
a new function for kallikrein-like proteins in the endocrine pancrea
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

hK6/hk10 may be involved not only in insulin processing, but also in glucagon, somastotin, pancreatic polypeptides and other pancreatic hormones, as well as serotonin, which may be involved in pancreatic islet cell function.
hK6/hk10 may be implicated in the processing and/or secretion of pancreatic hormones.
hK6 is a kallikrein, but hK10 is not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hK6 is a new pancreatic kallikrein, which is expressed in the islets as well as in ducts of the pancreas, while hK10 is a kallikrekin, which is expressed only in the islets.
hK6/hk10 are involved in insulin processing, and possibly other pancreatic hormones, and that the kallikrein family is involved in the physiology and pathophysiology of the pancreatic islets.
kallikrein-related peptides may be important regulators in the endocrine function of the pancreas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
kallikrein 10 and 6 may be involved in hormone processing and secretion, as well in physiological functions related with the pancreas.
the expression pattern of kallikrein 6 and kallikreine 10 is similar to that of the other kallikreines in the human pancreas.
kallikrein-6 and kallikreine-10 are expressed throughout the islets of the pancreas and are co-expressed with the hormones of the pancreas.
